newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish millers sell 40,000 T flour to Libya.
newsitem.headline: Turkish millers sell 40,000 T flour to Libya.

text.p: Three Turkish millers have agreed with Libya to sell it 40,000 tonnes of wheat flour with November and December shipments, officials from the miller companies said on Thursday.

"The total amount is 40,000 tonnes by three millers. We are now waiting for letters of credit to be issued through a Swiss bank," said an official from Uncular Besin Mills, one of the three exporters.
"I expect the deals to be finalised soon," he told Reuters.
He said the Ankara-based Ankara Un Sanayi would sell 30,000 tonnes to Libya and his company, Uncular, based in Tekirdag in western Turkey, would sell 5,000 tonnes.
Ankara Un was not immediately available for comment, but the independent Turkish Millers' Association confirmed Ankara Un's deal.
Tarik Gencer, general manager of the Marmara Un Sanayi miller firm, also based in Tekirdag, said his company would also export 5,000 tonnes to Libya.
The Uncular official said the sales would be around 410 Swiss francs per tonne on a cost and freight basis.
Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan left Ankara on Wednesday for a tour of Egypt, Libya and Nigeria, and said Turkey would boost trade ties with those countries.
His trip to Libya was criticised by some members of his coalition partners because of alleged comments by Libyan Leader Muammar Gaddafi that Turkey was persecuting the Kurds in its southeast.
Gencer said the flour export deal to Libya had nothing to do with Erbakan's trip. "The agreement was made long before we knew of his (Erbakan's) trip," he said.
